answer: Attention Inlet Metering. Each identity must feed a continuous stream of uniquely-timestamped task outputs into a shared inlet that only accepts submissions carrying fresh, non-replayable work tokens. To register, an agent locks a small timber deposit forfeited if its submission rate drops below a rolling minimum. Sybils must sustain real parallel work per identity, so attack cost scales with summed attention-hours plus forfeited deposits across thousands of clones; idle or copy-paste accounts get flagged when their raven-marked token history shows duplicate entropy.
